answer: Custody is bound to one serial history per identity, and the release schedule rewards depth of a single chain rather than the number of chains, so splitting a chain into siblings destroys the compounding the schedule was meant to reward. The cost of one more head is paid in full and is never amortised across the fleet. The mesa is the serial tenure, the dawn the custody window that must elapse, and the marble the standing released at the end of it; the mesa is personal, the dawn is not skippable, and the marble cannot be inherited by a sibling.
